PREFACE 
  I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & 
Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its beha lf, present this Two Hundred Thirteenth 
Report on the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences on the recommendations contained in Two Hundred Fourth 
Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2010-2011) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences. 
2.  The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences on the recommendations 
contained in the Two Hundred Fourth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & 
Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2010-2011) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences which was 
presented to the Rajya Sabha on 22nd April, 2010. 
3.  There were twenty three recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Fourth Report of the Committee. Action Taken 
Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Ministry on 23rd July, 2010. 
4.  In the meeting held on 8th December, 2010 the Committ ee considered the draft Action Taken Report and adopted the 
same. 
 
 
 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY
 
NEW DELHI; Chairman, 
December 8, 2010 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
  Science and Technology, Environment and Forests. 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
REPORT 
  The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences on the recommendations 
contained in the Two Hundred Fourth Report of the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & 
Technology, Environment & Forests on the Demands for Grants (2010-2011) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which was 
presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 22nd April, 2010. There were twenty three recommendations in the Two 
Hundred Fourth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from 
the Ministry on 23rd July, 2010. 
  The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the action taken by the 
Ministry of Earth Sciences are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:– 
MECHANISM DEVELOPED TO MONITOR AND REVIEW THE ONGOING SCHEMES 
Recommendation (Para 4.3) 
  The Committee notes with concern that inspite of having  the existing mechanism to m onitor and review the ongoing 
schemes, some of the programmes, such as India Meteorological Department; National Centre for Medium Range Weather 
Forecast; Polymetallic Nodules Programme; Development of Manned  Submersible, Gas Hydrates etc. which were undertaken 
by the Ministry during the last three years particularly 200 7-08 and 2008-09 witness under utilization of funds. The Committee 
recommends the Ministry to furt her strengthen this mechanism for effective impl ementation of its programmes so as to avoid 
delay in the implementation of various projects and also in avoiding underutilization of the funds allotted to it. The Committe e 
also recommends that the Ministry should avoid procedural and administrative delays through efficient planning and 
management. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and would like to know the details of initiatives taken by the Ministry to strengthen 
its monitoring mechanism. The Committee reiterates that Ministry must stre ngthen its mechanism to monitor and 
review the ongoing schemes for timely utilisation of funds. 
ELEVENTH FIVE YEARLY PLAN-OUTLAYS AND PROPOSALS 
Recommendation (Para 5.3) 
  The Committee takes a very serious view of the fact that the Ministry has grossly underutilized the allocated budget of the 
first three financial years of the Eleventh  Five Year Plan which shows only slackness and laxity on the part of the Ministry. 
When the Committee enquired about the sorry state of affairs in respect of utilization of allocated funds, the Secretary admitt ed 
that trend of expenditure has not been upto the mark, and one of the reasons for this is that the Ministry was setup only in 20 06. 
It is also true that planning was not that good but they have  improved this year and assure the Committee that their performance 
will be very good next year. The Committee is not at all convinced by the lame excuses given by the Ministry as most of them 
are administrative and procedural in nature which could have been avoided by efficient planning and better monitoring of 
schemes/ projects. The Committee therefore, recommends that the Ministry must plan its programme in such a manner that it 
may be able to utilize the allocated funds in the financial year  itself. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry show 
improvement in its utilization trend this year so that it could convince the Committee as well Planning Commission for 
additional allocation in future. 
Action Taken by Government 

  The Ministry had taken up adequate measures to strictly monitor (monthly) the phase of expenditure for accomplishment 
of the financial targets. The Ministry has developed an appropriate mechanism to achieve the financial milestones set for the 
current financial year. After achieving the half-yearly targets, the Ministry proposes to approach for additional funds. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and is of the view that th e Ministry should have provi ded the details of adequate 
measure taken to strictly monitor the expenditure for accomplish ment of the financial targets. The Committee is also of 
the view that the Ministry should make  use of these measures to meet the fi nancial targets of the current year and 
ensure that Planning Commission releases necessary additional funds as per requirement. 
BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR 2010-2011 
Recommendation (Para 6.4) 
  The Committee notes that some major schemes such as m odernization of India Meteorological Department, Climate 
Change Centre, Polar Science are likely to be affected on accounts of cut imposed by the Planning Commission while allocating 
funds to the Ministry. Even ongoing schemes are not accorded prio rity in fund allocation. The Committee is of the view that 
with reduced budgetary support it would not be easy for Ministry to pursue its programme vigorously. The Committee 
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should take up the issu e of additional fund allocation at R.E. stage for new schemes, 
with the Planning Commission, in right earnest and impress upon them the need for such higher allocation, indicating the 
seriousness of the Ministry to achieve its targets. The Committee,  at the same time also recommends that Ministry should also 
plan its projects/schemes meticulously so as to avoid any dr astic cut in their projections because of poor performance in 
utilization of previous funds. 
Action Taken by Government 
  India Meteorological Department: The recommendation of Committee has been noted for compliance. 
  Polar Science: For the Polar Science Scheme, allocated budget is less compared to the projected demand. At the RE stage, 
the Ministry shall take up the issue of additional funds for the scheme as per the requirement during 2010-11. At present the 
scheme is implemented as per envisaged programme. During 2009-10, the budget utilization was almost 100% (99.96%) under 
this scheme. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and expresses its satisfac tion that the Ministry was able to fully utilize the 
budgetary allocations under the Polar Science Scheme during the year 2009 -2010, but at the same time it is of the view 
that it must accord same priority to other schemes also while utilising the allocated funds. 
OCEAN OBSERVATION AND INFORMATION SERVICES 
Recommendation (Para 7.1.7) 
  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry needs to enhance its scientific and technological capabilities in respect of 
predicting tsunami and earthquakes since accurate observations and advance warnings about these natural hazards could give 
enough time to disaster management agencies to be better and timely geared up to minimise the loss of property and lives. 
Action Taken by Government 
  Noted for action. Ministry has started implementing a Nati onal Programme on Earthquake Precursors (NPEP) in a pilot 
mode to capture and understand possible earthquake pre-cursory characteristics over selected regions during the Eleventh Five 
Year Plan. Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Servi ces (INCOIS), Hyderabad has further strengthened its tsunami 
warning centre during 2010 (Jan-July). 
 

Comments 
  The Committee notes that the Mini stry has started implem enting a National Pr ogramme on Earthquake 
Precursors (NPEP) to understand possible earthquake pre-cursory characteristic s over selected regions during the 
current Five Year Plan. 
Recommendation (Para 7.1.8) 
  The Committee notes that the Ministry has initiated a de dicated programme on Ocean Biogeochemistry of the Northern 
Indian Ocean which has been proposed during the mid-term stage of the Eleventh Five Year Plan. The Committee hopes that 
the Ministry would attain the objective of the programme and would successfully conduct multi-disciplinary biogeochemistry 
studies in the Indian Ocean with a view to understand fluxes of material of both micro and macro nutrients as this could be 
important to understand the impact of climate change on the oceans and to understand the living resources in the Indian Ocean. 
Action Taken by Government 
  Recognising the importance of Ocean Biogeochemistry for understanding towards climate change and ocean biological 
resources, the Ministry had taken up an initiative at Mid-Term Stage of Eleventh Five Year Plan. 
  A project proposal was prepared and appraisal has been completed for seeking approval. After obtaining the approval, 
project has been launched from the current financial year. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply.  
Recommendation (Para - 7.1.9) 
  The Committee has observed that Rs. 25 crores has been provided for Indian National Centre for Ocean Information 
Services (INCOIS) to provide services and conduct in house R&D projects. The Committee recommends that services of 
INCOIS may be optimally used to provide ocean information and advisory services to society, industry, Government agencies 
and scientific community through sustained ocean observations, information management, modeling and constant 
improvements through systematic and focused research. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The Ocean Information services being rendered by INCOIS Hyderabad to various stake holders is primarily aimed to the 
societal benefit. This information has been generated and disseminated using a wide range of state-of-the-art technology 
observing platforms, modeling and systematic research. Efforts have been launched to utilize the resources optimally. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply.  
Recommendation (Para - 7.1.10) 
  While the Committee appreciates the progress made by the Ministry in respect of providing fishery services to the 
fishermen about the potential fishing zone and the state of the ocean which has become highly popular among the fishermen. 
However, while fishing in the deep sea, it so happens that sometimes fishermen inadvertently happens to cross maritime 
boundary and venture into the boundaries of other countries. The Committee in this background enquired from the Ministry 
whether any system has been or is being developed to warn our fi shermen not to go beyond the particular point, which is Indian 
maritime boundary. To this, the Secretary replied that an experiment has been initiated in association with Space Applications 
Centre of ISRO to develop an instrument to warn the fishermen and it is expected that an instrument would be developed 
shortly. The Committee recommends that efforts should be made to develop that instrument at the earliest, so that fishermen 
may not be arrested and prisoned for crossing international border while fishing in deep sea. 
Action Taken by Government 

  The Ministry has conducted an experiment in associatio n with Space Applications Centre of ISRO to develop an 
instrument to warn the fishermen and it is expected that an instrument would be developed shortly. 
  INCOIS in partnership with industry has developed on a pilot basis an “Integrated GPS & Radio Information System 
(IGRIS)” to help the fishermen community in all the above aspects. The IGRIS fitted on-board the fishing vessels will 
comprises a GPS location-cum-vessel navigation system which is very useful for better navigation of the vessels. As IGRIS 
enables a two-way communication, it will be extremely useful fo r fishermen especially in distre ss. Presently, efforts are now 
underway to develop a low cost portable unit for the above with other industry partners. 
Comments 
  The Committee appreciates the actions undertaken by the Ministry in associ ation with Space Applications Centre 
of ISRO to develop an instrument to warn the fishermen not to go beyond part icular point. The Committee hopes that 
the Ministry will be able to develop the low cost portable instrument for the use of fishermen at the earliest. 
NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF OCEAN TECHNOLOGY 
Recommendation (Para 7.2.4) 
  The Committee has observed that, National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) demons trated the Low Temperature 
Thermal Desalination technology by commissioning of a plant of 1 lakh litre per day capacity and produced fresh water at the 
first trial run at the North Chennai Power Plant during last year  by using waste heat from Power Plants. Besides, three more 
desalination plants of 1 lakh litre capacity one each are being setup at Minicoy, Agatti and Androth islands of Lakshadweep 
islands. The Committee appreciates the fact that the Ministry ha s done the commendable job in the area of desalination of sea 
water. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry must work hard to make such plants cost  effective which can contribute 
significantly to the needs of the population of these islands. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should expand and 
extend this programme so that safe drinking water could be provided to the communities living around the coastal areas. The 
Committee appreciates that the Ministry is also exploring the possibility of Public-Private Partnerships for further developmen t 
of the technology and hopes that it will achieve its goal in this regard in future.  
Action Taken by Government 
  Thanking the Committee, the Ministry had conducted experiments to optimize the cost of the production of seawater. The 
Ministry has embarked on establishment of desalination plants through the public-private partnership to commission 
desalination plants in various major islands of Lakshadweep as well as near the thermal plants located on the coast of India. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and desires that the Minist ry should keep trying to optimize the cost of the 
desalination of seawater. 
GAS HYDRATES AND TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT FOR EXPLOITATION 
Recommendation (Para - 7.3.6) 
  Gas hydrates with their abundant resource potential is likely  to emerge as a potential clea n fuel resource. The preliminary 
assessment of geological condition and limited available seismic data suggests high possibility of occurrence of large quantity  
of gas hydrates within the EEZ of India. The Committee is of the view that it has the potential of providing total energy security 
to our nation on account of its widespread occurrences and potential energy content. To meet the overwhelming demand of 
energy in the country it can be looked as an alternate source of energy as well as a clean fuel. The Committee feels that it is  
necessary to carry out various geological, geochemical and ge ophysical analyses systematica lly for the identification and 
quantification of gas- hydrates along the continental margins of India for evaluating the resource potential. 
Action Taken by Government 
  A suitable scientific Research Vessel has been identified and chartered to carryout multi channel seismic survey. Detailed 
multi channel seismic survey is being carried out in Krishna Godavari (KG) and Mahanadi basin by Indian scientists. 

Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and woul d like to know the details of the ou tcome of the multi channel seismic 
survey carried out by the scientific Research Vessel. 
Recommendation (Para 7.3.7) 
  The Committee hopes that the Ministry would take concerted efforts to develop the technology for extracting gas from 
gas hydrate accruing below the seabed at  100-200m and will achieve success in produ cing gas hydrates in large quantities. The 
Committee feels that adhoc and token approach of the Ministry reflected in allocations made during the years 2007-08 and 
2008-09 under this programme would lead us no where. The Mini stry needs to focus and concentrate on this programme more 
vigorously. The Committee therefore, recommends that the Ministry should take gas hydrat e as a pilot project so as to intensify  
its efforts to this project and exploit its potential resources in the national interest in a time bound manner. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The Ministry has identified two promising sites (one at Krishna Godavari (KG) basin and other at Mahanadi basin) for 
detailed study. The multi channel Seismic Study has been commissioned in a mission mode to understand the physics of 
occurrence, its spatial distribution etc. The assessment of resource potential and development of technology for its exploratio n 
are also part of this mission mode endeavour. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and opines that Ministry sh ould ensure that all its existi ng technological facilities 
are utilised to their utmost capacity so as to derive maximum understanding of the gas hydrates. 
Recommendation (Para 7.3.8) 
  The Committee notes that non availability of suitable proposals for selecting and hiring of research vessel to carry out 
multi channel seismic survey and delay in identifying a suitable joint partner for the development of autonomous coring system 
led to the underutilization funds during the previous two years of Eleventh Five Year Plan, however during last year the 
Ministry has found a suitable su rvey vessel and research activities could be commissioned in this regard. The Committee feels 
that the Ministry must take corrective meas ures to avoid such delays in future and take every possible step to utilize the budg et 
in the financial year itself to avoid non-utilization of allocated funds. 
Action Taken by Government 
  Noted. 
  There was a delay in commencement of multi channel seismic survey due to delay in identification of suitable scientific 
research vessel through global tender. However, now, the problem ha s been solved and a suitable research vessel was charted. 
Autonomous Coring System (ACS) has now been integrated and currently undergoing sea trials off Chennai coast by National 
Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai. In future, advance action would be taken for chartering of vessels to avoid re-
occurrence of such delay. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and opines that Ministry shou ld stick to its objective a nd must plan its actions well 
in advance to avoid procedural delays in future. 
POLYMETALLIC NODULES PROGRAMME 
Recommendation (Para - 7.4.3) 
  The Committee is of the view that th e greatest unexploited mineral resources on  the earth are on the deep sea floor 
including manganese nodule, cobalt rich manganese crusts containing nickel, copper and hydrothermal deposits that contain 
copper, lead, zinc, gold and silver. Since India is endowed with  a vast Exclusive Economic Zone of about 2.02 million sq. km., 
the Committee feels that the Ministry should approach its projects  related to identification and exploitation of ocean resource s 
in a well focused manner to meet the requirements of minerals and make concerted efforts towards developing technology for 

sufficient metal recovery from the polymetallic nodules and tapp ing rich resources from ocean since the country needs large 
scale mineral resources for its industrial growth. 
Action Taken by Government 
  Regarding polymetallic nodules from deep seabed, extensive research & development work have been undertaken. The 
resource potential has been established through extensive survey and exploration at Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB). 
  The development of demonstration of pilot mining system for operation upto a water depth of 6 km has been planned by 
the Ministry in phases. As a first phase of development, National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) has designed and 
developed a prototype shallow bed mining system capable of working upto a depth of 500 m. The system has been 
demonstrated successfully at a depth of 451 meters in the Arab ian Sea off Goa. Development of integrated mining module with 
collector and crusher is under progress. 
  Process package for extraction of metal from nodule has been validated though a pilot plant demonstration of 500 kg/ day 
capacity which is first of its kind of demo plant in the world.  The metal recovery efficiency was more than the expected 
capacity of plant. The R&D improvements in certain section of the process route are in progress. The other process package 
development work is also under progress. The survey and ex ploration work in the areas of cobalt crust & hydrothermal 
sulphides are also in progress to identify the site and to assess the resource potential.  
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply with satisf action that the Ministry is doing acti vities in developing mining system 
for operation upto a water depth of 6 km and has achieved a bed mining system capable of working upto a depth of 500 
m. The Committee hopes that Ministry wo uld keep doing such activities and enha nce its capability of extracting metal 
from, the nodules. 
Recommendation (Para - 7.4.4) 
  The Committee, however, notes with concern that the Ministry has failed to fully utilize the allocated budget during the 
last three financial years i.e. 2007-08, 2008-09 and 2009-10. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry must not 
show any slackness in utilizing the enhanced budget allocated for this financial year. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The Ministry had taken up adequate measures to obtain cl earances for launching slated in first 3 years of Eleventh Five 
Year Plan and strictly monitor the phase of  expenditure for accomplishment of the financial targets. The Ministry has built in 
appropriate mechanism to achieve the financial milestones set for the current financial year. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and is of the view that inspite of taking up adequate measures and strict 
monitoring of phase of expenditure, Ministry had not been able to fully  utilize the allocated budget for the first three 
financial years of the Eleventh Five Year Plan. The Committee reiterates that Ministry must make concerted efforts to 
utilise the allocated funds to meet its targets. 
POLAR  SCIENCE 
Recommendation (Para 7.5.5) 
  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry should u ndertake every possible institutional and logistic activity in 
respect of establishment of third permanent Indian Base at Lars emann Hills and it may also aspire for yielding positive results  
as substantial amount of funds has been approved towards activities associated with Polar Science. The Committee recommends 
that some target date should be fixed for completing the task, as in the absence of any time-frame, the project may lose its 
importance. 
 
 

Action Taken by Government 
  Activities for establishment of 3rd permanent Indian Station were initiated during the 29th Indian Antarctic Expedition. 
All the heavy cargo including 50 ton crane, dozers, vehicles, li ving modules etc. have been stationed at the proposed 
construction site. The approach road from landing site to construction site has been completed as also the helipads. The firm f or 
the construction of the phase 1 of the project has been finalized. 
  The project is targeted to be completed by the end of Eleventh plan period. Considering the extremely adverse working 
conditions in the polar regions as also the small window of approx. 112 working days in a year, phase wise target date and 
event-wise target date has been fixed to complete the project in time. 
Comments 
  The Committee expresses its satisfaction that the Ministry has initiated approp riate activities for establishment of 
third permanent Antarctic Research Statio n. At the same time, Committee desires that the Ministry should ensure that 
the project progresses as per its time schedule and gets completed by the end of Eleventh Five Year Plan as envisaged by 
it. 
Recommendation (Para - 7.5.6) 
  The Committee further recommends that equipping the existing  Indian station ‘Himadri’ in Arctic with field equipments 
and processing units and continuing long term approved scien tific projects which are the proposed activity under Arctic 
Programme, should be pursued diligently and in a well-planned and strategic manner and the data collected from its scientific 
expeditions to Arctic must be analysed to understand the changes in. glacier position in the north pole. 
Action Taken by Government 
  Since the first Scientific Expedition to Arctic in 2007, Indian Arctic Expedition has been undertaken annually in three 
phases (two summer & 1 winter). International Arctic Research facilities available at Ny-Alesund are being utilised by the 
scientists for the research purpose. Indian station ‘Himadri’ is being equipped with processing units & equipments. 
  The following scientific activities are being pursued: 
  Study of polar ionosphere; Measurement of atmospheric electr ical parameters to understand global electric circuit; Carbon 
cycling in the nearshore acquatic environments; Multiproxy palaeoclimatic studies on quaternary deposits at Ny-Alesund; 
Parameterisation of glaciers in northern hemisphere to variations of climate inter annual and intra annual; Diversity of 
heterotrophic bacteria in Arctic water and sediment; Sulphur cycling in the Arctic environment - Changes in the sulphate 
reducing activity with fluctuation in temperature; Diversity of Arctic cyanobacteria. 
  Some preliminary results are as below: 
(i)  Initial investigation and comparison of data vis-a-vis that of August 2008 has shown a marginal recession of Vestre 
Broggerbreen glacier. Part of the glacier is being observed  for the last 3 years and as such no conclusive comment 
may be made on its behavior/position. 
(ii)  Observations of thin cyanobacterial mats were reco rded during the beginning of summer which gradually becomes 
thicker and darker in colour. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and would like the Ministry to keep collecting data and analyzing the changes in 
the glacier position. 
INDIA METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT 
Recommendation (Para - 7.8.4) 
  The Committee takes a very serious note of the fact that while the Ministry has grossly under utilized the allocated budget 
of the previous years under modernization of India Meteorological Department programme and this year it is submitting that the 

programme is going to be affected due to s hortage of funds. The Committee is constrained to observe that that this shows lack 
of seriousness and apathy towards utilization of allocated funds.  The Committee is of the view that reasons such as delay in site 
preparation for various observing systems and delay in delivery of long-lead items could have been avoided by efficient 
planning and better monitoring of project components at regular interval. The Committee feels that the Ministry must plan its 
programme in such a manner that it may utilize maximum percentage of allocated funds in the financial year itself so that there  
should be minimum carry forward of the unspent balance to th e next financial year. Therefore, the Committee recommends that 
there should be timely infusion of funds in various schemes/projects and the Ministry should evolve a suitable mechanism for 
optimum utilization of funds. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The recommendation of Committee has been noted for complia nce. Ministry has directed DG, IMD to expedite progress 
so that the time over-run is minimized. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and is of  the view that merely directing the co ncerned official of Department to 
expedite progress is not suffici ent on the part of the Ministry. The Committ ee opines that Ministry  should ensure that 
appropriate initiatives must be taken by  the concerned department for efficient planning and better monitoring of the 
project. 
Recommendation (Para -7.8.7) 
  The Committee feels that weather forecast and its accuracy  has today assumed greater si gnificance, specially, in the 
context of climatic changes taking place which have resulted in vagaries of monsoon and weather. Since, agriculture has 
traditionally been the cornerstone of Indian economy, scanty and sporadic rainfall during monsoon witnessed during the recent 
years has started adversely affecting agricultural production. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The observations and concerns of the Committee have been noted. Upgradation of weather forecasting systems including 
installation of radars, high performance computing and shifting to a numerical weather prediction model are at an advanced 
stage and targeted to be fully completed by end of the Eleventh Plan. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and desires that Ministry should take every step possi ble for timely dissemination 
of data to all stakeholders and utilize these weather forecasting systems to their best of abilities. 
Recommendation (Para - 7.8.8) 
  The Committee is of the view that the initiatives being take n by the Ministry to improve th e accuracy of weather forecast 
are welcome steps. The Committee however recommends that all th e processes and steps as indicated by the Ministry must be 
put in proper place as soon as possible and preferably before the onset of the coming monsoon so that predictions could be more 
and more accurate and precautionary measures to deal with flood like situation can be taken in advance. It also recommends that 
besides making consistent efforts towards achieving accuracy of monsoon forecast, it is also imperative to disseminate the 
prediction to the remote and far flung areas of the country so that it reaches the poor and marginal farmers also. The Committe e 
also recommends that the Ministry must ensure this year that  the funds allocated for modernization of India Meteorological 
Department must be fully utilized.  
Action Taken by Government 
  The recommendations of Committee have been noted for compliance. Appropriate steps have been taken to utilize 
maximum allocation of funds under modernization of IMD. 
Comments 

  The Committee notes the reply and would like to know the de tails of appropriate steps taken by the Ministry to 
utilize the maximum allocation of funds under the modernization of India Meteorological Department. 
DOPPLER WEATHER RADARS 
Recommendation (Para - 7.9.2) 
  The Committee observes that the Ministry’s contentions that  radars were imported because of its requirement being very 
high does not hold good on two grounds. Firstly, because the im ported radars are yet to be installed and secondly because there  
was delay in shipment of Doppler Weather Radar during 2008-09. As such, the Committee finds that the sense of urgency 
shown in import of radars got defeated. The Committee feels that instead of deciding to import radars from China, the Ministry 
should have persuaded BEL to manufacture more radars as it ha s rightly done now. The Committee therefore, recommends that 
the Ministry should try its best to make use of indigenous technology as it gives fillip to Indian industry and generate 
employment opportunities. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The recommendation of Committee has been noted for compliance. Global tender for supply of 12 S-Band Doppler 
Weather Radars was floated on 30-5-2008. There were seven venders including BEL. M/S Beijing Met star China was finally 
selected for supply of the Radars. All equipments have been received and are under various stages of installation. However the 
supply orders for 2 Doppler Weather RADAR was placed with BEL in March 2006 with delivery schedule in March 2008. BEL 
could deliver the Radar in March 2010 & June 2010 only. This RADAR is also under installation. 
Comments 
  The Committee takes note of the reply.  
CENTRE FOR CLIMATE CHANGE 
Recommendation (Para - 7.10.2) 
  The Committee feels that climate change re search is quite significant in the presen t context and it must not be allowed to 
suffer at any cost. It, therefore, recommends that the Ministry must continue with the ongoing and proposed activities related 
with this scheme and seek additional provision at the RE stage from the Ministry of Finance. 
Action Taken by Government  
  Noted for Action 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and wo uld like to know the details of progress made in the climate change research. 
INDIAN INSTITUTE OF TROPICAL METEOROLOGY 
Recommendation (Para - 7.11.4) 
  The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Earth Sciences has initiated a new programme on global and regional 
climate change and has successfully set up dedicated Climate Cha nge Research Centre with the state of art research facilities. 
This is indeed a timely initiative. The Committee recommends that all out effort should be made to enhance the weather, 
monsoon and climate prediction ability of this Centre for making reliable projection of weather and monsoon and the services of 
the Centre could be utilized to deal climate change issue in a holistic and comprehensive manner. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The recommendation of Committee has been noted for compliance. 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply a nd would like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard. 

NATIONAL CENTRE FOR MEDIUM RANGE WEATHER FORECASTING 
Recommendation (Para 7.12.3) 
  The Committee is of the view that thrust of weather forecasti ng must be on its accuracy and there is a need to ensure 
higher degree of precision in our weat her forecasting system. The Committee recommends that Ministry has to widen its 
objectivities and work hard to ensure the c onstant up gradation of forecast techniques and models for prediction with the use o f 
available, reliable and accurate satellite data. It appreciates that its products are provided to various agencies in the Gover nment 
and other users in a number of socio-economic sectors. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The recommendation of Committee has been noted for compliance. (Also Action Taken at Para 7.8.7 above may be seen). 
Comments 
  The Committee notes the reply and woul d like to know the initiatives take n by the Ministry to widen its 
objectivities and upgradation of weather forecast techniques. 
Recommendation (Para - 8) 
  The Committee is of the view that the Mi nistry of Earth Sciences which aims to look at the planet in a holistic way to 
understand the interplay of earth dynamics and systems phenomenon is striving to emerge as a knowledge and information 
technology enterprise for the Earth System Science. It has been doing commendable job of using science and technology for 
exploration and exploitation of vast marine resources for the socio economic benefit of the society. Given the commendable 
work, the Ministry of Earth Sciences is doing, the Committee st rongly recommends that the Mini stry of Earth Sciences should 
be properly and adequately funded and any kind of reduction in outlay at R.E. stage should be strictly avoided as far as possible. 
Action Taken by Government 
  The Ministry expresses gratitude for the appreciation. 
  The vision of the Ministry is to excel in knowledge and technology enterprise for the earth system science (atmosphere, 
biosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere and ge osphere) realm towards socio-economic bene fit of the Indian Sub-continent and in 
the Indian Ocean region. The primary mission is to develop scie ntific understanding of the Earth System to improve prediction 
of climate, weather and natural hazards for the Indian sub-cont inent and in the Indian Ocean Region. Long-term measurements 
of variables to record vital signs of the Earth system, Conduct focused process studies, Development of Earth system models, 
Development of an information system and services for societal, environmental and economic benefits. 
Comments 
 The Committee notes the reply.
